money_at_stake.rationale: The occurrence, per the signal's own occurrence block, is the broader humanoid-robot volume-production crossing (assembly plus the actuator/gearbox layer that gates it), not the actuator layer alone. The only market-size forecast that survived direct verification in this evidence-discipline pass is MarketsandMarkets' USD 5.41bn (2026) growing to USD 50.27bn by 2035 at a 28.1% CAGR: comfortably above the USD 10bn floor of B10_100 well before the occurrence's own 2028-2031 window closes (CAGR-extrapolated from the same cited 2026 base and rate, this points to roughly USD 18-30bn across that span) and short of the USD 100bn floor even at the 2035 terminal year. The Goldman Sachs Research figure carried in the prior version of this appraisal (a USD 38bn base case and USD 154bn blue-sky scenario) could not be verified this run: the Goldman Sachs page returned HTTP 403 on direct fetch and no Wayback Machine snapshot was reachable through this session's tools, so that citation is dropped rather than carried forward unverified. Band: B10_100, now resting on one verified source rather than two independent convergent ones, a real reduction in evidentiary depth this appraisal's review_by should revisit if a second citable forecast becomes reachable.

public_reach.rationale: The pool splits the same way the occurrence's own thesis splits it. The actuator/gearbox supply layer the signal names as the unmapped link is close to entirely listed: Harmonic Drive Systems and Nabtesco on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Green Harmonic on Shanghai's STAR Market, all three named suppliers in the signal's own evidence. The OEM/assembly layer is genuinely mixed and moved in this appraisal's favor during the review window: Tesla is listed (already the retail story, but still a reachable listing), and Unitree, the highest-volume 2025 producer per the signal's own evidence, converted from private to a freshly listed, heavily-traded STAR Market stock (up as much as 629% intraday, closing around USD 53bn market cap) eleven days before this appraisal. Figure AI, Apptronik and Agility Robotics, the other named OEM deployers per the signal's own evidence, remain privately held; this pass deleted the one citation this appraisal previously carried for a Figure AI private valuation (the source did not contain that claim, see changelog), so that slice of the OEM pool is now reachable-unknown rather than assigned a dollar figure. Scored 60, the 'clearly reachable, mixed' anchor, rather than higher because a real slice of OEM-side value still sits outside any listing even though this appraisal can no longer size it.

capture_odds.rationale: Revised down from the prior two-sided 50 after this pass deleted the item that supplied the 'against capture is not hypothetical' half of the argument: a claimed 4.3% trailing operating margin against a 10.7% industry average. The actual Harmonic Drive Systems source states operating margin recovered from 'effectively zero' a year earlier to 11.0% this quarter, with 11.4% full-year guidance, and states no industry-average figure anywhere in the article: neither number in the deleted claim was real, so it is deleted rather than repaired (see changelog). What survives is one-sided: a well-capitalized Chinese competitor, Suzhou Green Harmonic, already holds over 35% of the global harmonic-reducer market and over 60% domestically while pricing 40-60% below the Japanese incumbent, which is the textbook mechanism for competing margin away once the current scarcity phase resolves into a multi-source, price-sensitive market. Absent a surviving citation for the incumbent's own margin trajectory, this appraisal cannot weigh that pricing threat against a demonstrated counter-fact, so it is scored 40, 'some specs, mostly price-taker,' rather than the prior 50.

timing_fit.rationale: Revised down from the prior 85 after this pass deleted two of the three supporting items. One claimed Harmonic Drive Systems management guided 'humanoid-related order contribution to reach a considerable level from FY2027 onward'; the actual source discusses AI robots generally, with one North American customer's roughly JPY 1.2bn order and a vaguer expectation that 'one or two more customers producing at the scale of 10 or 100 units will emerge over the next one to two years,' not a distinct FY2027-onward humanoid commitment, so it is deleted rather than softened to fit. The other, an LP Information harmonic-reducer-for-humanoid-robot market forecast to 2031, returned no fetchable page content on two direct attempts and had no reachable Wayback Machine snapshot, so it is deleted as unreachable. What survives is Nabtesco's new RVmini/Monocrank reduction-gear lines, launched and slated for exhibition at iREX2025 (December 3, 2025) citing humanoid and collaborative robots as a demand driver, squarely inside the occurrence's own window (anchor_date 2026-02-01, roughly 2028-2031). That is one dated, in-window, supply-side data point rather than the convergent order-guidance-plus-market-forecast picture the prior version claimed, so it is scored 60, 'credible inside the window,' rather than 85.

notes.text: REACHABLE, not LEAKY: this occurrence is the mirror image of the Arctic case. The dominant supply-side names the signal itself flags as unmapped (Harmonic Drive Systems, Nabtesco, Green Harmonic) are already listed, and the OEM side gained a major reachable name mid-appraisal when Unitree IPO'd on 2026-08-19. The open question a chain build should target is capture, not reach: Green Harmonic's 40-60% underpricing of the Japanese incumbent, on a base of over 35% global market share, is a live threat to margin on exactly the link this signal calls the retail gap. This appraisal no longer carries a citable number on the incumbent's own current margin trajectory (a prior figure claiming 4.3% trailing margin against a 10.7% industry average did not survive source verification and was deleted 2026-08-30), so a chain build should treat the margin-defense side of this question as open and worth its own sourcing rather than settled.
